root.claim: A deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, with $p$ bits of working precision, $d$ transform axes of length about $r$.
root.method: Reduce the product to a convolution through a chain of representation changes, evaluate it with the two fast tape procedures, then recover the exact product and sum the costs

motivation.text: Multiplication is a convolution of digits, convolution is computed by transforms, and the cost of transforms is dominated by address movement and butterflies, so a power saving in those two procedures gives a power saving in the whole product.
